search_bias: evaluation/verifiers; adaptive proposal triage versus confirmation evidence; fresh-audit firewall; stagewise type-I accounting; expected audit cost

public_sources.title: Safe testing
public_sources.authors: Peter Grunwald; Rianne de Heide; Wouter Koolen
public_sources.used_scope: Conditional e-variables can be constructed just before the next fresh study using all prior information, and their running product remains safe under optional continuation when the conditional e-variable property holds. Used to justify conditioning the fresh confirmation test on the entire proposal/development history.

public_sources.title: Preserving Statistical Validity in Adaptive Data Analysis
public_sources.authors: Cynthia Dwork; Vitaly Feldman; Moritz Hardt; Toniann Pitassi; Omer Reingold; Aaron Roth
public_sources.used_scope: Adaptive reuse of analysis data changes validity conditions; a protected holdout can validate adaptively chosen analyses when its information flow is controlled. Used as background for separating proposal-generation data from a fresh/protected confirmation stage, not as a direct e-process theorem.

public_sources.title: The reusable holdout: Preserving validity in adaptive data analysis
public_sources.authors: Cynthia Dwork; Vitaly Feldman; Moritz Hardt; Toniann Pitassi; Omer Reingold; Aaron Roth
public_sources.used_scope: Publicly documented holdout principle: unrestricted adaptive exploration can be separated from protected validation. Used as conceptual support for the confirmation firewall.

arbitrary_dev_screen_fresh_confirmation_.setup: Let H contain the entire reused-development history, arbitrary adaptive proposal-generation transcript, chosen candidate h(H), and an arbitrary audit-trigger G(H). After h is frozen, draw fresh confirmation data. Assume that for every realized H for which h(H) is null/non-improving, the fresh confirmation e-process F_t satisfies P(sup_t F_t >= 1/alpha | H) <= alpha.
arbitrary_dev_screen_fresh_confirmation_.bound: P(G(H)=1, h(H) null, fresh confirmation passes) = E[1{G=1,h null} P(pass | H)] <= alpha E[1{G=1,h null}] <= alpha.
arbitrary_dev_screen_fresh_confirmation_.consequence: The development screen can be arbitrarily adaptive, overfit, and statistically invalid as a test and still consume zero confirmation type-I budget, provided it is used only to decide whether to spend fresh audit resources. It must not contribute evidence to commit, and the candidate/test specification must be frozen before fresh confirmation outcomes arrive.
arbitrary_dev_screen_fresh_confirmation_.scope_guard: This is per confirmation opportunity. Repeated adaptively chosen candidates need run-level multiplicity/error spending. It also fails if fresh outcomes leak back into candidate generation before the candidate's commit decision or if the claimed conditional fresh-null validity is false.

stagewise_error_accounting_taxonomy.OR_rule: If either of two valid stages can independently authorize a false commit, a general safe bound is alpha1+alpha2 (or a sharper dependence-aware bound when justified).
stagewise_error_accounting_taxonomy.AND_confirmation_rule: If the same fixed/null candidate must pass stage 1 and then a conditionally valid independent/fresh stage 2, P(false commit)<=alpha1*alpha2; the stage-2 bound is conditional on all stage-1 history.
stagewise_error_accounting_taxonomy.TRIAGE_rule: If stage 1 only decides whether stage 2 is run and cannot authorize or numerically strengthen the commit evidence, stage 1 does not need an alpha allocation at all; final per-opportunity false-commit risk is controlled by stage 2 alone.
stagewise_error_accounting_taxonomy.measurement_rule: Record which stage can alter the candidate, which stage can authorize commit, and which evidence is mathematically multiplied/merged. 'Two-stage validation' is too ambiguous to determine the correct error accounting.

fixed_candidate_AND_cost_power_stress.setup: Global alpha=.05, maximum 50 fresh tasks, same structured (.80,.60) Bellman design in each stage. Search B1 in {5,10,...,45} and alpha1 .08-.40 with alpha2=.05/alpha1, requiring both stages to pass. Compare against one-stage at matched boundary risk.

simulation_expected_tasks.simulation_trajectories: 60k-80k per condition; expected stopping includes early threshold crossing and stage-2 launch only after stage-1 pass.

fixed_candidate_AND_cost_power_stress.interpretation: Hard AND confirmation was substantially less powerful at matched false-commit risk but used fewer expected fresh tasks. Its value is therefore a compute/throughput trade rather than a free statistical-power improvement in this tested fixed-candidate setting.

free_dev_triage_full_fresh_audit_stress.setup: Treat a 10-task development screen as already-sunk/non-confirmatory data, then give every triggered candidate a full independent 50-task fresh confirmation at alpha=.05. Screen thresholds are labeled by their alpha-like crossing threshold only for simulation; their validity is irrelevant to the theorem because they cannot commit.
free_dev_triage_full_fresh_audit_stress.interpretation: Triage reduces how often expensive fresh audits run and correspondingly reduces both useful commits and false commits. Unlike an AND split of a fixed 50-task fresh budget, it does not need to weaken the fresh confirmation threshold just to account for an invalid adaptive development screen.

new_or_updated_candidate_findings.mechanism: Allow unrestricted/adaptive development and proposal screening, but require candidate freeze before an independent/protected fresh audit. Only the fresh conditional e-process may authorize commit; development statistics can decide whether an audit is worth paying for but receive no evidential credit unless separately selection-corrected.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.evidence: Direct conditional-probability proof plus Safe Testing conditional e-variable principle and adaptive-data holdout literature. In the worker-local stress test, arbitrary screening traded audit volume for resolution without consuming confirmation alpha.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.scope_guard: Per-candidate/opportunity only; repeated confirmations require a run-level error budget. Freshness/protection must be real, and candidate/judge/test specification cannot adapt to the confirmation outcomes before decision.

new_or_updated_candidate_findings.mechanism: Make the control plane declare stage semantics as OR-authority, AND-confirmation, or TRIAGE-only before allocating type-I budget. Use sum-like, product-like, or confirmation-only accounting respectively under the stated conditional-validity assumptions.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.evidence: Elementary conditional probability bounds; fixed-candidate two-stage simulation shows materially different power/cost behavior from one-stage testing.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.scope_guard: Dependence, shared samples, candidate mutation, or reused confirmation information can invalidate simple product accounting; stage labels must be backed by actual dataflow provenance.

new_or_updated_candidate_findings.update: Two-stage architecture adds expected audit cost as a third Pareto axis. A lower false-commit rate from a hard AND gate is not automatically preferable if the same risk can be achieved by one-stage alpha tightening with substantially higher deadline resolution.

rejected_or_narrowed_generalizations: Rejected: 'every development/proposal screen that affects whether a candidate is audited must consume part of the statistical alpha budget.' Not if it cannot authorize commit and fresh conditional confirmation alone controls the decision.

Rejected: 'two alpha-valid stages should always split alpha by Bonferroni.' OR, AND, and triage-only semantics have different valid accounting; an AND sequence can have a product bound, while a pure triage screen can have no confirmation alpha allocation at all.

Rejected: 'fresh confirmation automatically solves the whole adaptive loop.' It solves candidate-selection validity for that confirmation opportunity under the stated freeze/freshness conditions, not run-level multiplicity over many candidate confirmations.

Narrowed: 'two-stage confirmation is statistically stronger because it requires replication.' In the tested fixed-total-budget case it was less powerful at matched false-commit risk; its advantage was lower expected testing cost and stronger architectural separation.

Narrowed: 'a dev screen should be calibrated as a hypothesis test.' For triage-only use, ranking audit value/cost can matter more than nominal dev-set type-I error, because validity comes from fresh confirmation.

frontier.action: Extend the fresh-confirmation firewall from one opportunity to an adaptive stream of candidates. Let audit launch times and per-audit alpha_j depend predictably on all past development/audit history, require a pathwise global alpha-spending rule, and compare geometric spending, fixed-count Bonferroni, and e-value closed/online alternatives under correlated candidate quality.

Optimize triage for expected value of information rather than dev p/e-value: predict fresh-audit pass probability and candidate harm/value from development-only features, then choose audits under a fresh-task budget while keeping those predictions out of commit evidence.
Compare protected reusable-holdout mechanisms against truly fresh confirmation when fresh tasks are scarce, accounting for every validation-derived side channel and selection transcript.
frontier.scope_guard: Do not treat generic reusable-holdout theory as automatically compatible with the paired-sign e-process; derive the actual interface.

frontier.action: Add rare catastrophic safety endpoints and multi-endpoint commit rules so average paired-sign confirmation cannot hide low-frequency severe regressions.

exact_next_action: Formalize run-level alpha spending for an adaptive sequence of fresh confirmation audits: allow arbitrary development-driven audit triggering and candidate generation, but require each candidate be frozen before its audit and choose alpha_j predictably with the pathwise sum of launched-audit budgets <= alpha_global. Prove any-false-commit control, then compare spending schedules on a stylized repeated-candidate stream.
